hook: In a superconductor, a hidden spin supercurrent can cancel a resistive spin current, theory shows.
summary: Spin currents usually fade by losing angular momentum to relaxation. The authors show that a superconductor with a spin-splitting field can instead carry an opposing condensate spin current, so total spin and charge currents vanish. This is a theoretical result, and the proposed spin-to-charge signals have not been measured.
title: Hidden Spin-Supercurrent Counterflow in Conventional Superconductors
